claims.claim: English conversion or zero derivation includes canonical cases in which a lexeme is used in another word class without an overt derivational affix, including noun-to-verb conversion.
English word-class membership is identified from grammatical behavior and distribution, and many forms can belong to more than one word class, as with book as noun/verb and fast as adjective/adverb.

entries.notes: R44 audit: la explicación de conversión sin afijo y la necesidad de identificar la categoría por el comportamiento gramatical son correctas para el nivel B2. Los ejemplos water, empty, email y back ilustran adecuadamente la multifuncionalidad; las reglas de distribución se presentan como heurísticas pedagógicas y no alteran el núcleo conceptual. claims.claim: English has major word classes including nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs, and many words can belong to more than one class depending on their grammatical use.
Forms such as book and fast provide standard examples of category alternation: book can be noun or verb, while fast can be adjective or adverb.

entries.notes: R44 audit: la entrada comunica correctamente que una misma forma puede pertenecer a varias categorías y que el contexto sintáctico ayuda a desambiguarla. Las caracterizaciones semánticas de cada clase son simplificaciones introductorias, pero los ejemplos y la explicación de distribución evitan convertirlas en una prueba única. PASS_NO_CHANGE. claims.claim: Common nouns refer to classes or categories, whereas proper nouns name specific entities and are conventionally written with an initial capital letter.
English conventionally capitalizes days of the week, months, and names of languages.

entries.notes: R44 audit: la distinción común/propio, los ejemplos y la regla de mayúscula son correctos. La observación sobre días, meses e idiomas coincide con la convención ortográfica estándar del inglés. PASS_NO_CHANGE. R33 canónico sigue pendiente.

claims.claim: Concrete and abstract are semantic noun classifications: concrete nouns denote material or perceptible entities, whereas abstract nouns denote non-material notions such as ideas, feelings, qualities or situations.
Abstractness does not determine countability; abstract nouns can be countable or uncountable, and some nouns shift countability with meaning and context.

entries.notes: R44 audit: la entrada separa correctamente la oposición concreto/abstracto de la oposición contable/incontable, usa idea e information de forma pertinente y reconoce cambios de interpretación como paper. PASS_NO_CHANGE. R33 canónico sigue pendiente.

claims.claim: Countable nouns can occur in singular and plural forms, combine with a/an in the singular, and combine directly with numerals and quantifiers such as many or a few.
Countability is a grammatical property that can vary by sense; nouns such as information and advice are characteristically uncountable in standard English.
